result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_windmill_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a windmill graph Wd(k, n) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6068-L6162){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_windmill_graph( n, k, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Windmill graph](/assets/graphs/add-windmill-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three windmill graphs side by side, each a hub shared by several blades: three triangles (the friendship graph) for n=3 and k=3, four triangles for n=4, and three complete graphs on four nodes for k=4. Blades meet only at the hub, so removing it leaves n separate pieces." width="100%"} Creates `n` complete graphs ("blades") of `k` nodes each that all share one hub node. The graph has `n(k - 1) + 1` nodes and `n * k(k - 1)/2` edges. The hub is a cut node joined to everything, and removing it leaves `n` separate cliques of `k - 1` nodes. With `k=3` the result is the friendship graph (`n` triangles sharing a node), and with `k=2` it is a star. The hub is created first, then the other `k - 1` nodes of each blade in turn. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one, so the hub's edges all point outward. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Windmill graphs are useful for: - modeling overlapping groups that share one member (a person who belongs to several otherwise separate teams) - test cases for articulation points, biconnected components, and overlapping community detection, where the hub belongs to every group - the friendship theorem: graphs in which every two nodes have exactly one common neighbor are exactly the friendship graphs ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of blades (cliques). Must be at least `2`. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each blade, counting the shared hub. Must be at least `2`. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; the hub gets the first number. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` or `k=` is less than `2`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three triangles sharing a hub (the friendship graph) have `7` nodes and `9` edges: ::: {#737da287 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_windmill_graph(n=3, k=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (7, 9) ``` ::: ::: The hub, node `"1"`, is the only articulation point; removing it leaves three separate edges: ::: {#29fb78e9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_articulation_points(), graph.delete_node("1").count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([1], 3) ``` ::: :::
